matches.note: Billed "Jakks VS Mike Kenada"; "Winner: Jakks". Fought in the cage and ended on a ten count: the count runs to "Ten" over Kenada, who "wasn't getting up", and Jakks "exited the cage door".
"Riot was forced to tap out!" — "Winner: Araknis".
A ten count after the "Bull's Horn"; "Winner: Amp Canon".
"Winner: Brandon Blade".

date.source: the fed's own event archive: "Sunday Night Flaw 02: 03-31-2002"

appearances.note: Billed in the tag match but never came out; appears in two scenes, dragged out of a Taco Bell to be debuted and knocked down on the ramp by Xaxon.
At a graveside, where he phones the owner to say he cannot make it that day.

matches.note: Billed "Vicious Circle VS Riot and Avo Chavez". Avo Chavez's theme played, "But nothing happened", and Vicious Circle went after Riot alone; Riot "tapped out" to their finisher, Torture, and Vicious Circle walked to the back, "victorious". Riot's later hunt for "a man that had seemingly abandoned him in their tag team match" confirms the no-show.
The page declares no result: Riot ran in with a garbage can and attacked both men as "the referee called for the bell".

Billed "Jakks VS Quincy Brown" and fought in the cage. The page has no "Winner:" line; the winner is read from the finish: "Both men collapse on the mat", the count runs to nine, Quincy "sluggishly gets to his feet...barely missing being counted as knocked out", the "10!" is called and "Jakks didn't share his fate", and Quincy alone leaves the cage. Sunday Night Flaw 06 recalls this fight as "ending in the former picking up the win" (Quincy Brown).
"Lennox's hand was raised in victory."

date.source: the fed's own event archive: "Sunday Night Flaw 03: 04-07-2002"

appearances.note: Present and silent while his manager talks with Noah Krone backstage: "The two newest additions to thReat walk down the hall in stride".

matches.note: "The match was over! Xaxon won the match."
Billed "Amp Canon VS Jakks"; Jakks "was declared the winner via knockout."
Riot "laid over top of his nearly dead enemy, and the referee made the count": "3!"

date.source: the fed's own event archive: "Sunday Night Flaw 04: 04-14-2002"

appearances.note: Runs in from the crowd and kicks at the back of Xaxon's legs, shaking his bitten manager in Xaxon's face.
Introduced in a locker-room vignette that ends "Who am I?" / "Disciple X".

matches.note: Billed "phYre VS Jakks". A cage fight: WildphYre "sent Jakks down and out" and the count runs to "10"; "phYre was making his statement and Jakks did not earn his number one contendership". The page has no "Winner:" line.

A cage fight with no "Winner:" line; the winner is read from the sequence of the finish, not from a result line: Quincy's "right hook!" lands, the ten count runs, and at the bell "Quincy Brown stumbled out of the cage" while "Amp crawled through the cage door leaving a trail of blood".
"Noah Krone pulled out a quick victory."
"Riot covered him" for the three count. The fed's title history dates Riot's Aggression Championship win over Lennox Dawson to this show.

date.source: the fed's own event archive: "Sunday Night Flaw 05: 04-21-2002"

appearances.note: Attacks Noah Krone from behind outside the arena while his manager looks on, and later runs down with a chair in Krone's match with Riot.
In his office as Araknis presses for an Aggression Title shot; he ends the meeting with "Now I've got to make a phone call".

matches.note: A pole match: Avo Chavez's bitten manager "hung 15 feet above the ring canvas" and the bell rings when Xaxon, out of the ring, "laid his weak hand on top of the soft shell manager, and grasped it": "The match was over with age and experience winning this battle."
Disciple X "wrapped him up for the pinfall."
"phYre was declared the winner."
"The referee ends the match! Double Count out!"
Three count; "the referee lifted his arm in victory."

date.source: the fed's own event archive: "Sunday Night Flaw 06: 04-28-2002"

appearances.note: Arrives at the arena and gives his name to a security guard: "I'm Steven Solex".
Arrives in a rusted Gremlin, unnamed in that scene, and meets the owner backstage: "I'm August Monday, I own your Fighting Championship".

matches.note: Takisuma Ogama rolled Disciple X on top of Noah Krone and woke the referee, who made the count: "3!"
"Dawson beat CashnMoney!!" CashnMoney's earlier covers are kicked out of or broken up at the ropes; Dawson then "did his finisher, Purposes!!!" and the count runs "1", "2", "3!!"

Billed "Quincy Brown VS Jakks"; after the ten count "the referee declared a no-contest, as both bloodied fighters stayed rooted to the canvas." A cage fight: Quincy "made his way to the cage" and the two fought "inside the cage".

Riot "hooked one of Ogama's legs, as the referee made the count": "3!!!" Ogama's manager, Bobby Blair, threw in a steel chair and Noah Krone leapt in to give Ogama "one last chair shot to the spine": "Due to the assistance of Noah Krone, the Aggression Champion had prevailed".

date.source: the fed's own event archive: "ReLoad 2002 PPV: 05-05-2002"

appearances.note: Debuts after the World Title match: the lights go out, "GOD IS NOWhere" appears on the screen, and he stands over a beaten Disciple X and names himself, "I am Gabriel Oliver Danielson. I am GOD."

Read as Kid Jive from the text's chain of names: a fan who heckles CashnMoney from the crowd, hops the railing during the cage match with Lennox Dawson and comes into the cage to brawl with him, under the same name as the man who signs a contract on Sunday Night Flaw 07, whom Sunday Night Flaw 08 names as Kid Jive.

matches.note: "August Monday wins the match by Knockout".
"Takisuma wins the match by Igniting".
"Lennox Dawson wins the match by Exiting".
"Riot wins the match by pinfall".
"Quincy Brown wins the match by Knockout".
"Xaxon wins the match by pinfall".

appearances.note: Answers Riot's open challenge and loses the Aggression Championship match.
A new signing who signs a contract giving him "minor booking powers" and books himself against J.J. $tudd, leaving the owner's office as "Jive"; Sunday Night Flaw 08 names the same man Kid Jive.

matches.note: "Steven Solex wins the match by Knockout".
Billed "phYre vs. Jakks"; "No Contest".
"Araknis wins the match by Submission".

Billed "??? vs. Riot". Riot, "the Aggression champion", asks for someone to "face me for the Aggression title"; Lawrence Clamentia comes down and after "1..." "2..." "3." Riot is "still the Aggression champion": "Riot wins the match by pinfall". A defence of the Aggression Championship.

notes: The fourth match is headed "??? vs. Riot"; the opponent is named in the text.

appearances.note: Sits silent beside his manager backstage until Araknis walks in: "Takisuma just looks at him, blank faced".

matches.note: "Winner: Monday via Submission".
"Winner: JJ $tudd by DQ" — CashnMoney attacked Studd.
"Winner: Clamentia via Pinfall".
Billed "Disciple X VS G.O.D. VS Xaxon"; "Winner: No Contest".

appearances.note: In his office as Disciple X demands a match with Vince Jacobs; he books it for the next week.
Debuts by walking down the ramp with a microphone, "It's time you get face to face with me, Rejection", and brawls with Noah Krone.

matches.note: Billed "phYre vs. Jakks"; "Winner: Jakks via Knockout". A cage fight: Jakks opens by "ripping a bat off the side of cage" and phYre goes for "a chair from the cage wall".
"Winner: August Monday via Knockout". A cage fight: Monday "walks into the cage" and Solex goes "to the cage wall" for barbed wire.
Billed "Lawrence rejection vs. Riot"; "Winner: Riot via pinfall". The fed's title history records Riot giving the Aggression Championship to Lawrence Clementia on this show.
"Winner: Frank Nock via Knockout". A cage fight: "in our cage", with weapons taken from "the cage wall".

Billed "G.O.D. vs. Disciple X"; "Winner: Disciple X via pinfall". A lumberjack match, "the first in the history of thReat"; the lumberjacks are Vince Jacobs and Xaxon, who join in on Disciple X, and White Lightning distracts Jacobs so that Disciple X can win.

date.source: the fed's own event archive: "Sunday Night Flaw 10: 06-02-2002"

appearances.note: Interferes in the International Title match, chairing Riot from the crowd in a long black coat; also in a locker-room scene with his wife.

Read as Kid Jive from the text's chain: "Jive" runs through the curtains after CashnMoney's power bomb on J.J. $tudd, chairs $tudd out of the ring and brawls with CashnMoney up the ramp; CashnMoney's challenge to "Jive" for a cage match next week is the cage match Sunday Night Flaw 11 stages as CashnMoney vs. Kid Jive.
Interferes in the Disciple X v Vince Jacobs main event: clocks the referee and hits a bulldog on Disciple X before White-Lightning's bat.
Interferes in the main event with a baseball bat to G.O.D.; also in Disciple X's hallway and locker-room scenes.

Appears in two scenes: stumbling out of the costume area drunk, called "Conan" by Joey Starr in the hallway, then in the ring with an open challenge that only the jobber Pete Extreme answers; he beats Extreme with a steel chair and a somersault leg drop, and Joey Starr comes out and beats him down.
Takes a phone call about Xaxon and Quincy Brown backstage and runs out, pushes through security to Xaxon, and screams at Quincy Brown just before a chair hits Quincy from behind.

matches.note: "A ten count was ensued, and Solex was victorious."
"Rejection had won his debut match."

Billed "Takisuma Ogama -c- vs Riot". A defence of the International Championship: Ogama is billed as the champion, "-c-", and has "his title buttoned around his waist". Riot has Ogama hooked for a reverse DDT, the prelude to the Crowd Control, when a man in a long black coat hops the rail with a chair and hits Riot in the face, and his coat opens on Araknis; "The referee called for the bell as security rushed in". Ogama locks in the Ogamacity, Riot's face "turned purple", and Ogama walks out and grabs his belt, "Confident in the fact that he had earned this win". The page has no "Winner:" line and names no pin, submission or count; the winner is read from Ogama leaving with the belt.

Billed "J.J. $tudd vs. CashnMoney". The page declares no result: after CashnMoney's power bomb Jive runs out, chairs $tudd out of the ring and brawls with CashnMoney up the ramp until security "controlled the situation".
Billed "Disciple X vs. SVJ"; after the three count "Disciple X rolled off of SVJ".

name: Sunday Night Flaw 11

date.source: the fed's own event archive: "Sunday Night Flaw 11: 06-09-2002"

appearances.note: Appears first on the big screen in a message to Joey Starr, then in person: he walks through the crowd into the ring, knocks Starr off the top rope and swings a chair at him, and is beaten down and cut open with his own bottle.

matches.note: "It was all over Rejection won the Aggression Title!!" — the Aggression Championship, Lawrence Clamentia defending.

A cage fight: the cage is lowered around the ring, Monday hits phYre with a chair, a fire extinguisher and the Rage Within, and the count runs to "10!!!" with phYre out. The page has no "Winner:" line; the winner is read from the sequence of the finish, and Monday is then stitched up in the first-aid room.

The page has no "Winner:" line and no count. Kid Jive falls through a table after a jump from the top of the cage, and CashnMoney hammers the chained cage door open and "walked out of the cage!": leaving the cage is the win, so the winner is read from the sequence.

The referee "called for the bell, determining Araknis the winner by DQ." Bobby Blair, Takisuma Ogama's manager, runs out with a chair and swings it at Riot twice; Riot pulls Araknis in front of the second. The match is headed "Takisuma Ogama banned from Ringside" and Ogama does not appear.

Quincy Brown speaks after "a hard fought win over Steven Solex". A cage fight and a defence of the Fighting Championship by Quincy Brown, "the defending champion": he hands the belt to the official inside the cage. Each man takes a count to nine; the finish is Quincy's right hook and "SHOOT EM IN THE HEAD", and "Ten seconds later" he "has successfully defended his title". No closing count is narrated.

Billed White-Lightning vs. "Superstar" Vince Jacobs; "Vince had gotten his hand raised as the winner of the match." Victoria Jacobs is at ringside with Vince. After the count Disciple X, freed from the fake police, charges the ring and trades blows with Vince until the StarStruck lays him out.

Joey Starr's in-ring debut, billed against “a thReat legend”; Pete Extreme comes out instead, dressed as a leprechaun, and the Leprechaun himself later breaks in. Starr hits the Starr Stunner (a hurricanrana variation) onto glass from a booze bottle, “makes the cover and gets the win over the jobber”, then puts the Leprechaun through a table and hits the Five Starr Frog Splash.

notes: Unlisted bout: Joey Starr against Pete Extreme in a green suit, entering to the Leprechaun's music; the page has no "Winner:" line, but Starr takes the cover after the Starr Stunner: "Joey makes the cover and gets the win over the jobber".

the fed's own event archive: "Sunday Night Flaw 13: 04-06-2003 - ARCO Arena, Sacramento, CA"

appearances.note: In his dressing room, arguing with the bodyguard his father sent to protect him, then storming out to show he needs none.
Introduces himself on video: he sets a camcorder on a tripod in his locker room to "broadcast" himself, and it falls over twice.

Not named on this show: read as Ty Hughes, appearing as the masked "El Crackerooni", a new Mexican signing who pretends not to understand English and leaves the arena in a cab. Sunday Night Flaw 15 has Vincent Pembridge pull the mask off "EL CRACKEROONI" to reveal "TY HUGHES", and Flaw 16 says Hughes had been "impersonating" him for weeks.

matches.note: "Winner: J. Leslie Voss via pinfall".
"Winner: Wolf via submission".

"Winner: Disciple X via pinfall".

appearances.note: Leads the robed Faithless in a candlelit vigil with Marcus Escobar.
Comes out with a microphone to mock Sanders, then hits him with the vPlex so that Pembridge can cover.
A new signing who is turned away at the door, gets backstage by using a fan's dash over the barrier as a distraction, and is thrown out for not being on the list.
Takes a phone call in his office and accepts an offer to wrestle, then leaps from the crowd in the Royale v Anthony match, knocks Anthony off the turnbuckle and splashes him.

Not named on this show: read as Ty Hughes, appearing again as the masked "El Crackerooni", who has lost his mask and arrives at Troy Mason's office with a paper bag over his face, dances on Mason's desk and puts the mask back on backwards. The unmasking on Sunday Night Flaw 15 names him "TY HUGHES".

matches.note: "Winner: Wolf via submission".

"Winner: Vincent Pembridge via pinfall". J. Leslie Voss comes out with a microphone to mock Sanders and hits him with the vPlex; Pembridge, who has kept the referee's attention, then hits a release German suplex and covers for the three.

"Winner: Resch Royale via count-out". The winner line says "via count-out", but the narrated finish is a pinfall: Ric Graves works the referee out of the ring, nØt leaps in from the crowd, splashes Anthony and drapes Royale's arm over him, and the referee comes back and counts "1....2....3!!"
"The bell rang as did Jason's heart. His first win." Sarah Marie Knowen, Kyle Knowen's wife, chairs the referee and then her own husband and drapes Semps over him for the three count.

"Winner: Vincent Pembridge via submission". Maria Manetta, Dane's sister, comes out behind him. Pembridge pushes the timekeeper off his chair, hits the referee with it and chairs Dane, then chokes him "out cold" until the referee calls the match.

Billed as “the most anticipated match in wrestling history”: Bobby Knickerson's first wrestling match, against the sixty-year-old janitor Earl Stinkovich. Stinkovich bursts into tears, jumps out of the ring and runs up the ramp; the bell rings “signalling a count-out victory”. “Winner: Bobby Knickerson via count-out”.

notes: Unlisted bout: Against Earl Stinkovich; "Winner: Bobby Knickerson via count-out".

name: Sunday Night Flaw 15

date.source: the fed's own event archive: "Sunday Night Flaw 15: 04-20-2003 - American West Arena, Phoenix, AZ"

appearances.note: Runs down in the Voss v Knowen match and spears Kyle Knowen, then takes a superkick from Sarah Marie Knowen; also in the main-event brawl on the Vagabonds.
With Marcus Escobar when Joshua Smith tries to chat her up backstage, and Escobar steps in behind him.
Comes out with Troy Mason's Resistance in the closing brawl on the Vagabonds.
On a taped promo from a house on the Flaw Vision, with his brother Beau: the two, "collectively known as Extreme Impact", say they have signed with thReat.
On a taped promo from a house on the Flaw Vision, with his brother CJ: the two, "collectively known as Extreme Impact", say they have signed with thReat.

matches.note: "Winner: Jason Semps via pinfall".

Billed "J. Leslie Voss vs Oooh, Mystery!"; the page's own credits name the match "J. Leslie Voss vs Kyle Knowen". "Winner: J. Leslie Voss via pinfall". General David Sanders runs down and spears Kyle Knowen instead of Voss; Sarah Marie Knowen, Kyle's wife, superkicks Sanders out of the ring, spin-kicks Voss and superkicks her own husband unconscious, and Voss covers the knocked-out Knowen for the three.
"Winner: Dane Manetta via pinfall".
"Winner: Fire via pinfall".

Maria Manetta, Dane Manetta's sister, makes her wrestling debut after a challenge earlier in the night, against the newcomer Chris Pinash, also debuting. Pinash clocks her across the back of the head with a root beer can the referee does not see and pins her: “Winner: Chris Pinash via pinfall”. Dane Manetta then challenges Pinash (the card's next match, order 3 here).

notes: Unlisted bout: Against Maria Manetta; "Winner: Chris Pinash via pinfall".

date.source: the fed's own event archive: "Sunday Night Flaw 16: 04-27-2003 - Alamodome, San Antonio, TX"

appearances.note: Chats up Vertigo backstage, comes to the ring during her cruiserweight title match, rolls her back in and swings a chair at Atken, and afterwards proposes to her and takes a low blow for it.
Cuts a promo asking Steve Solex for an Iron Man match at Malevolence, and jumps Solex backstage: "How about you fight back at Malevolence, huh?!"
Walks to the ring with Marcus Escobar and urges him on from ringside.
Comes down to ringside to chase Geneva and pulls Marcus Escobar's throat onto the top rope, so that Escobar trips over Bobby Knickerson.
Enters in a black suit and cuts a promo on Darren Anthony, until Anthony, out of the crowd, chairs him and sends him over the ropes.
Walks the corridors and is shouldered by a stranger, and tells him his name.

Not named on this show: read as blind from the text's chain of clues. A man paces the rafters above the crowd, "Completely blind to his existence", walks the halls for "his first sacrifice" and shoulders into Malik Roland, then leaves the building, "his job was done". Sunday Night Flaw 17 shows the man who attacks Malik entering to "Angel" by Massive Attack in a black trench coat and sunglasses and telling him "you are blind", and Malevolence 2003 announces "blind" to the same song, the same coat and glasses and the same line, "Beyond Lies Innocence, Not Death".

matches.note: "Winner: Marcus Escobar via pinfall". Geneva urges Escobar on from ringside; Joshua Smith comes down after her and pulls Escobar's throat onto the top rope so that he trips over Knickerson.
"Winner: General David Sanders via pinfall".

"Winner: Vertigo via pinfall". The match crowns the first thReat Cruiserweight Champion. Atken locks in Humiliation and Vertigo taps, but the referee has not seen it; Fire jumps onto the apron and then sneaks in with a chair and comes close to hitting Atken with it. Vertigo hits the Triple V Driver and pins him; after the bell Atken beats her down and takes the belt off her.
"Winner: Dane Manetta via knockout".
"Winner: Christian Embers via knockout".
"Winner: Ampske via knockout".

date.source: the fed's own event archive: "Sunday Night Flaw 17: 05-11-2003(05-04-2003) - Tad Gormley Stadium, New Orleans, LA"

appearances.note: Comes out on one crutch and breaks it over Wolf's head during the Escobar v Wolf match, then scampers off unhurt.
Joins the announce team and chairs Darren Anthony from behind in the Anthony v Ampske match.
Announced for their debut and never came: after a countdown gag the ring announcer says Extreme Impact was "unable to attend".
Opens the show in his office, comes down the ramp to cheer on Darren Anthony in the main event, and climbs in afterwards to name him the first member of the Resistance.

Brushes off Joshua Smith in the corridor and goes into her locker room, where Marcus Escobar is talking with Tyler Davidson; walks Escobar to the octagon; and takes on Christian Embers with the Faithless in the closing brawl.
Comes out with the Resistance in the closing brawl on the Vagabonds and takes on nØt and Bobby Knickerson.
Waits at the ramp with Christian Embers after Anthony's win and helps beat him down, then takes a beating from Dane Manetta in the brawl.

Not named on this show: read as blind. After Malik Roland's win a man in a black trench coat and sunglasses enters to "Angel" by Massive Attack, chairs Malik in the cage and tells him "you are blind"; Malevolence 2003 announces "blind" to the same song, the same coat and glasses and the same line, "Beyond Lies Innocence, Not Death".

matches.note: "Winner: Tyler Davidson via knockout".
"Winner: Malik Roland via pinfall".
"Winner: Malik Roland via knockout".

"Winner: Marcus Escobar via knockout". Geneva walks Escobar to the octagon and watches through the mesh. A fan in a "Wolf Sucks!" shirt draws the referee out of the octagon and Steve Solex breaks a crutch over Wolf's head while the referee is away; the ten count then runs over Wolf.

"Winner: Darren Anthony via pinfall". Troy Mason comes down the ramp to urge Anthony on. Ty Hughes and Bobby Knickerson join the announce team, and while the referee holds Knickerson back Hughes chairs Anthony from behind. Anthony wins with a small package after a low blow the referee does not see, and Mason climbs in to name him the first member of the five-man Resistance.

date.source: the fed's own event archive: "Sunday Night Flaw 18: 05-18-2003 - Birmingham Ice Arena, Birmingham, AL"

appearances.note: Appears on the Titan-Tron in Sanders' locker room wearing Sanders' dog tags; the distraction lets Fire low-blow Sanders.

Strips Phil Atken of both cruiserweight titles, comes out with Darren Anthony and introduces his tag partner, names Jason Semps as Pembridge's challenger and Quinton May as the fifth man of the Resistance.
With Marcus Escobar when Malik Roland comes looking for the man who attacked him.
Runs down and swings a chair at Darren Anthony, who blocks it, and with Ric Graves and the Vagabonds helps beat down Anthony and Semps.
Raps behind a locked locker-room door and is never seen: "They call me the Remix".
Comes out demanding Steve Solex, is ambushed from behind by him, and takes him out with the Jaws of Death.
Comes out on crutches, backs off when Wolf calls him out, then ambushes him from behind and counts the pin himself before Wolf catches him with the Jaws of Death.

Not named on this show: read as blind. A man stands on the roof above the arena studying a photograph that "reminded him of Malik Roland" and thinking of "the blind"; later the man who attacked Malik answers him from the screen with "Beyond Lies Innocence, Not Death" to the sound of "Angel". Malevolence 2003 announces "blind" to the same song and the same line.

matches.note: "Winners: Dane Manetta & Chris Pinash via knockout".
"Winner: Ty Hughes via knockout".
"Winner: Fire via pinfall". J. Leslie Voss, on the Titan-Tron in Sanders' locker room, taunts Sanders with his dog tags, and while the referee is watching the screen Fire low-blows Sanders.
"Winner: Phil Atken via knockout". After the finish Troy Mason comes down, takes both cruiserweight titles from Atken and pulls him from the Malevolence title match.

Billed "Chrsitian Embers & Ampske vs Darren Anthony & INTERNATIONAL MAN OF MYSTERY~"; the page's own credits name the second man Jason Semps. "Winner: No Contest". The text carries a rundown only: Troy Mason comes out with Darren Anthony and Ric Graves and introduces Anthony's partner, Jason Semps; the match is thrown out when all four men fight outside with weapons, and Graves and nØt, with Ampske and Embers, beat down Anthony and Semps.

"Winner: Vincent Pembridge via submission to win thReat Fighting Title". A cage fight: Pembridge brings out the thReat Fighting Title, stolen from Troy Mason's office weeks before, to "return from extinction", and Mason names Semps his challenger. Pembridge chokes Semps until he "tapped out".

matches.stipulation: thReat Fighting Title/ACW Scorpion Title Bout
matches.note: "In a draw." — "Winner: No Contest". A defence of the thReat Fighting Championship Pembridge has just won: Troy Mason makes him defend "your newly acquired thReat Fighting Title" against Quinton May. Quinton's piledriver leaves both men down and the ten count starts; Quinton gets to one knee, but Pembridge tackles him back down and the count reaches ten, "In a draw."

date.source: the fed's own event archive: "Malevolence 2003 PPV: 05-25-2003 - Philips Arena, Atlanta, GA"

appearances.note: Interferes in the ladder match, throwing Vertigo off the ladder as she reaches for the thReat belt; billed for the Showdown, he leaves the building rather than fight in it.
Walks out as the Resistance's fifth man, replacing Fire, and is the last man standing; afterwards claims he is still the World Champion, since the belt was never lost before the closure.
Talks his way past the Chief of Security at the arena door with his backstage pass, and the two smoke together.
Opens the show with a broadcast from his office, walks out with the Resistance as their "manager", and is speared by Ty Hughes when he slides into the ring at the end.
Raps in his locker room about the Showdown, face unseen.
Leaps out of the crowd with a steel chair during the Showdown and cracks Darren Anthony over the head, leaving before the referees see him.
A voice in the shadows, unseen: he plots to lure Jere Casarella to his side and signs off "psycho-Rio's back".

matches.note: The page's own result line reads "Result: WTHMFIH?~!!" No bell, referee or count: after the brawl on the ramp X-Ploder's "X-TERMINATE" flattens Bosnia's Finest, and Johnny Olympus, Born To Die's manager, pulls X-Ploder and SinFyre to the back.
Billed "-unknown- vs Malik Roland"; "Result: blind VICTORIOUS by pinfall."

matches.stipulation: Triple-Threat Ladder Match for the thReat Cruiserweight Title
matches.note: "Result: Phil Atken VICTORIOUS to become thReat Cruiserweight Champ." Fire throws Vertigo off the ladder as she reaches for the thReat belt, and Tyler Davidson takes the IOW belt instead; Atken retrieves the thReat title.
"Result: Chris Pinash VICTORIOUS via pinfall."

matches.stipulation: 30-Min Iron Man Street Fight for the thReat Aggression Title
matches.note: "Result: Solex VICTORIOUS by 5-4 to become thReat Aggression Champ."
"Result: General Sanders VICTORIOUS via pinfall." Troy Mason announces before the show that the match "is now a NO HOLDS BARRED MATCH"; the text calls it "Anything Goes".

A five-on-five between The Resistance and The Vagabonds as the page bills them; "Result: The Resistance." Fought as an elimination match. Fire, billed for the Resistance, leaves the building instead of fighting and Xaxon walks out as "the fifth and final member"; Xaxon covers Vincent Pembridge for the last elimination, after Ty Hughes spears Troy Mason and Karen Pembridge's hurricane kick puts her brother down. nØt chairs Darren Anthony from the crowd, and Troy Mason, who walks out with the Resistance as their "manager", slides into the ring at the end.

date.source: the fed's own event archive: "Sunday Night Flaw 19: 06-08-2003 - Tio Pepe Hall, Fort Campbell, KY"

appearances.note: Runs in with a French flag: strikes Ernie French, then Stephen Lee, and burns the flag over Ernie as the bell sounds for a no contest decision.
Opens the first segment after the satellite address with a promo on the man he beat at Malevolence: "One down. The rest of humanity to go."
Introduces himself to General David Sanders backstage ("My name is not of consequence to a lower being") and warns him, "this only makes me your newest nightmare".
Cuts a promo in the ring challenging Anubis for Jessica Jenkins's freedom; Anubis comes out with her on a leash and has her tell Levond he must put something of his own on the line.
Opens the show over a satellite feed ("this is a satellite broadcast"), explaining why he turned on Vincent Pembridge and closing "My job in thReat... is done."
Tackles Jason Semps from behind while Semps talks with his wife and manager, Sarah Marie Knowen, stomps him, throws his wedding ring at her and storms off.
Comes out to rap at the Kentucky crowd and is dropkicked out of the ring by Rent-A-Hero swinging from the rafters before he finishes.

Returns after a year away with a promo in the ring; Dane Manetta interrupts and they agree to meet next week, and Rejection hits him with a sit-down powerbomb and Inner Hatred: "REJECTION HAD RETURNED!"
Asks thReat's head scout why his application has not been answered and is told he is too big, cannot wrestle and "not too intelligent either".

matches.note: "Winner: nØt via pinfall".

"Winner: Ernie French via DQ". The page disagrees with itself: the narration has Jay Jaxxen run in with a French flag, strike Ernie French and then Stephen Lee with the pole and burn the flag over Ernie, and ends "The bell sounded for a no contest decision", while the closing line reads "Winner: Ernie French via DQ". The next show has Ernie say "if Jay Jaxxen hadn't attacked me, I would have won that match". The result here follows the page's closing line.
"Winner: Jere Casarella via pinfall".
"Winner: Steve Solex via pinfall to retain Aggression Title".
"Winner: Wolf via pinfall".

"Winner: Born To Die via pinfall". Born To Die's manager, Johnny Olympus, fights the referee through the match: he argues with him, pushes him and is pushed off the apron, pulls the top rope down as Stephen Martin is whipped into it, and pushes the referee again before the finish, so that the referee "slid across the canvas" as X-Ploder's X-Finisher on Nikal Dizdarevic is covered. Born To Die "had stolen their first win".

date.source: the fed's own event archive: "Sunday Night Flaw 20: 06-15-2003 - Galiano Arena, Louisville, KY"

appearances.note: Leads Marcus Escobar out for his match with Risto Dizdarevic and stays at ringside, steadying him on the ropes and holding Risto's foot down for the three count; later, as Marcus chains Nikal Dizdarevic backstage, she breaks a coffee pot over Risto's head.
Chases the driver who nearly runs down his companion and learns he is ORB, then with Sean Fury, in an orderly's uniform, straitjackets and abducts ORB from the ring.
Runs down the ramp late in blind's match with Rio Nexan and leaps back off the apron when blind goes for him.
The second "orderly": with Steven Fury takes ORB out of the ring in a straitjacket, then kicks him in the ribs in the car park before they drive off.
Comes out with "Twistodium" during Vertigo's match with Rent-A-Hero, distracting Vertigo; the referee swallows a tablet.
Ambushes General David Sanders in a car-park doorway without a word and beats him to the concrete; in a later locker-room scene Candor calls him "my soldier".
Passes Wolf backstage, then cuts a promo on the Louisville crowd about walking out on the Resistance at Malevolence and storms off.
In a locker-room scene with Vandal, tells him General David Sanders is "an impurity of the worst kind" and that he has done his bidding well.

matches.note: "Winner: No Contest". ORB unravels in the ring and talks to himself; two men in orderlies' uniforms run in, the taller kicks ORB, and they put him in a straitjacket and drag him out. The orderlies are Steven Fury and Sean Fury, "still dressed in the orderly clothes they wore when they nabbed ORB"; Steven's manager Mary Jane drives off with them.
"Winner: Rejection via pinfall".

"Winner: Marcus Escobar via pinfall". Geneva leads Marcus out and stays at ringside with Nikal Dizdarevic; she steadies Marcus on the ropes and holds Risto's foot down while Marcus's other leg hooks it, out of the referee's sight, for the three count; Nikal "had seen what Geneva did" and runs round the ring to stop it.
"Winner: Wolf via pinfall".

"Winner: Rent-A-Hero via pinfall". Twizzy comes out with a handful of "Twistodium" and distracts Vertigo; the referee, trying to remove him, swallows a tablet and goes "asleep" mid-count, then counts Rent-A-Hero's pin in "an extremely slow count".

"Winner: Rio Nexan via pinfall". DeVante Stevenson comes down the ramp late in the match and blind goes for him, and psycho-Rio's kick and implant DDT follow. The narration calls the man psycho-Rio throughout; the match billing and the closing line say Rio Nexan.

"Winner: Rio Nexan via pinfall". Anubis comes out with Jessica Jenkins on her leash while Levond draws a line in the mat, and Rio Nexan's Spinning Samoan Suplex takes Levond by surprise; Anubis then announces a match for Payback.

"Winner: Born To Die via disqualification". Johnny Olympus, Born To Die's manager, fights and pushes the referee and stomps Risto outside the ring; X-Ploder's fireball hits Risto, Nikal grabs the referee by the throat and slams him, and the referee "signaled for the bell". The narration and the closing line agree.

Billed "Tyler Davidson vs Phil Atken [c]". Tyler Davidson's theme is cut off and Phil Atken comes out alone with the Cruiserweight Title, says "there will be NO title defending tonight" and that Tyler is "sleeping in the back, with a dented chair over his head", and leaves: "Winner: No Contest". Tyler Davidson never appears; the title does not change hands.

name: Sunday Night Flaw 21

date.source: the fed's own event archive: "Sunday Night Flaw 21: 06-22-2003 - KU Rupp Arena, Lexington, KY"

appearances.note: Billed against DeVante Stevenson but never comes out; answers him from a live picture of the car park, where he blows up DeVante's car.
Waits in the ring for blind, who does not come out, and watches his own car blown up on the arena screens.

Charges out of the dark at Solex over the Neo-Nazi accusations and spears Denise Gomez instead when Solex pulls her in front of him; later plays the film he says will clear his name and is stunned by what it shows.
Sits at ringside with a chair during Jere Casarella's match with General David Sanders, drawing Jere's eyes, and slips away as it ends.
Run in after the count in Boris Fredrick Gastoff's match with Born To Die and beat Johnny Olympus with a double ankle lock.
Steps out of the dark to confront Stephen Lee in a boiler room.
Runs to the ring as haTE beats Sean Fury; later comes out with Mary Jane and is clotheslined and bloodied by ORB on the ramp.
Ambushes Steven Fury on the ramp with a clothesline, stomps and rams him into the wall and leaves as referees separate them.
With Vandal, taunts General David Sanders after Sanders's match with Jere Casarella, saying they are too far out of his league to grant him a match.
Stands beside Candor, silent, as Candor taunts General David Sanders backstage.
Debuts: interrupts Chris McCluskey's tirade against the crowd and challenges him to a debut match, giving him a week to answer.

matches.note: Billed "Boris Frederick Gastoff vs MYSTERY MEN~!"; the page's own credits name the match "Boris Frederick Gastoff vs Born To Die w/ Johnny O". The match is narrated to a three count for Born To Die: Johnny Olympus, their manager, pulls the referee over after a low blow, the Flaming Palm Thrust, the X-Terminator and SinFyre's "FIRESTORM!", "1... 2... THREE!", "a victory nonetheless for Born To Die"; the closing line reads "Winner: Born To Die via disqualification", though nobody is disqualified in the narration. Olympus jumps in with a jacket choke and a twisting lariat and pushes the referee into Boris's path; Generative Clash run in after the count and beat Olympus with a double ankle lock.

Billed "haTE vs ... Sean Fury?"; "Winner: haTE via pinfall". The referee rings the bell "pretty much for no reason at all. This match isn't schedualed"; Sean Fury comes out "without his mentor, Steven"; Steven sprints to the ring as haTE covers Sean and rolls in as haTE rolls out.
"Winner: Rejection via pinfall". Rejection comes out followed by his mistress Lucretia; Manetta knocks him off the apron with a baseball slide and Rejection ends it with "Rejected".

The page disagrees with itself: its narrative has "Sanders had just won big against Jere Cassarella", while the match's closing line reads "Winner: Rio Nexan via pinfall". The narration settles it for Sanders: the Last Surrender, "1… 2… 3!!", "The General had won" and the referee raises his hand, and "Sanders had just won big against Jere Cassarella". psycho-Rio never enters the match: he sits at ringside with a chair, drawing Jere's eyes, and has slipped away when it ends. The closing line names a man who is not in the match.
"Winner: Fire via pinfall".

"Winner: Tyler Davidson via count-out". Phil Atken makes his first title defence: he throws the title to the referee, kicks Tyler, and after a count that runs to ten with Atken outside the ring he leaves up the ramp with the belt; "Tyler had won the match, but not the title". Tyler Davidson's new manager (unnamed here) is introduced before the bell and is decked by Atken.

notes: The card's last billed match, "Singles Match blind vs DeVante Stevenson", is not a match: blind never comes out and answers DeVante from a live picture of the car park, where he blows up DeVante's car; "There was no match that night", and the closing line is a joke, not a result.

date.source: the fed's own event archive: "Sunday Night Flaw 22: 06-29-2003 - Conseco Fieldhouse, Indianiapolis, IN"

appearances.note: Comes out of the crowd during ORB's match with Steven Fury and hits ORB in the throat with a piece of metal.
Answers Solex's Nazi accusations: comes down the ramp to the crowd's "WOLF IS A NAZI" chant, spears Solex and is driven off by a low blow.
Cuts a promo that DeVante Stevenson breaks up with a baseball bat; later limps out of the arena refusing help.
Clocks Jere Casarella with a chair in his Aggression Title match with Solex, which Solex then wins; Jere storms after "his assailant, the infamous psycho-Rio".
Clotheslines ORB in a dressing-room brawl and tears at the cut on ORB's forehead until Mary Jane pulls him away.

matches.note: "Winner: Steve Solex via pinfall to retain Aggression Title". The match is a reporter's summary ("the transcriber's laptop crashed") and its finish is second-hand: Rio Nexan comes out and clocks Jere with a chair, Solex hits Jere with a piledriver on the same chair and takes the five count.

"Winner: Steven Fury via pinfall". Steven comes out with his manager Mary Jane, who distracts the referee on the apron; haTE comes out of the crowd and hits ORB in the throat with "a small piece of metal" before Steven's DDT on the concrete and the pin.
Billed "Candor & Vandal vs General David Sanders & Some Joker"; "Winners: Rent-A-Hero & General Sanders via pinfall".

date.source: the fed's own event archive: "Payback 2003 PPV: 07-05-2003 - US Bank Arena, Cincannati, OH"

appearances.note: Special referee of the Dungeon Match: steps between the two men and raises Steven Fury's hand.
Leaps the guardrail after Rent-A-Hero's match with Jere Casarella and attacks the hero until the Mecha Lariat puts him down.
Comes out with the World Title around his waist and introduces Xaxon before the cage match.
With Steven Fury and Mary Jane in the basement dungeon before the Dungeon Match, silent.
Trips General David Sanders and kicks him while Candor distracts the referee, then joins Candor's chair attack, for which Sanders wins by disqualification.

matches.note: Billed with "Paul Henry Davis" for PhD. All four men were counted out: "No Contest".
"Twizzy via pinfall".

"Steven Fury via lock-up". A Dungeon Match: "the winner is the one whom can lock one of these torture devices on his opponent". Steven Fury comes out with his manager Mary Jane, and Sean Fury is with them earlier in the dungeon; haTE is the special referee: he steps between the two men, and ORB trips over his foot before Steven shuts the Iron Maiden and haTE raises Steven's hand.
"Rent-A-Hero via pinfall". After the bell Remix leaps the guardrail in a throwback jersey and attacks Rent-A-Hero, who answers with the Mecha Lariat, and Remix retreats.
"Chris McCluskey via submission".

"Rio Nexan via pinfall". After the pin Jere Casarella runs down the ramp with a chain around his fist; psycho-Rio rolls out and taunts him up the ramp until the six men he had hired to attack Jere turn on him, and Jere leaps off the top rope onto Rio, who gouges his eyes and escapes into the crowd. The narration calls the man psycho-Rio; the billing and the closing line say Rio Nexan.

"Jason Semps via pinfall". Sarah Knowen, Kyle Knowen's own manager and wife, turns on him: she brings a chair into the ring, strikes his leg while he holds Semps in a full nelson, puts the chair round his ankle ("the ankle snapped"), and pulls the referee back in for the three count; she leaves with Semps.

matches.stipulation: Tag Team Rumble Explosion for the thReat Tag Team Titles
matches.note: "Born To Die via outlasting to become thReat Tag Team Champions".

Billed as Anubis; "Result: Anubis via pinfall". The masked "Anubis" who fights Levond Daniels from the bell is unmasked as Vincent Pembridge; a second masked man, "the second Anubis", comes from under the ring and pins Levond after a reverse death valley driver, and Pembridge then cuts a promo over him with Jessica Jenkins and a young man holding her leash. The text never names Kaysey Arrows and does not say which man is the Anubis of the earlier Flaws.
"Result: blind via pinfall".

"General David Sanders via pinfall". The page disagrees with itself: the narration ends with Vandal joining in, Vandal and Candor using a chair on Sanders, and "Referees poured to the ring to break up the mess, as the bell rang. Sanders had won via DQ", while the closing line reads "Result: General David Sanders via pinfall"; no pinfall is narrated. Vandal trips Sanders and helps Candor throughout.
"Rejection via pinfall". Rejection comes out with Lucretia, who throws him a chair as he stands over Manetta.

"Ernie French via submission". Before the bell Stephen Lee adds a stipulation: "if we lose… Our contracts are null and void, but if Ernie French loses then his contract is torn up"; after the submission both Lee and Jay Jaxxen are "released from thee threat roster".

matches.stipulation: No Holds Barred Match for the thReat Cruiserweight Title
matches.note: "Tyler Davidson via pinfall to become new thReat Cruiserweight Champion". The match is a simulcast from IWO's show, away from the Cincinnati arena; Tyler Davidson's manager (unnamed here) frees him from an armbar, slams the title belt across Atken's forehead before the Time Spike and points the cover out to the referee.

"Wolf via burning of flag to become new thReat Aggression Champion". A Flag Match: Wolf announces "Flag Match, baby. First person to retrieve the opponent's flag and burns it… wins"; he pulls Solex's flag from the turnbuckle, burns it and is given the title.

Billed "Xaxon vs TBA"; the General climbed out of the cage: "GENERAL MOTHERFUCKING DAVID SANDERS VIA CLIMB-OUT TO WIN THE MOTHERFUCKING THREAT WORLD CHAMPIONSHIP". A cage match: the steel cage is lowered over the ring; Troy Mason, holding the belt, introduces Xaxon, and Vincent Pembridge comes down with a sledgehammer, hands it to Xaxon and joins the announce team.

date.source: the fed's own event archive: "Sunday Night Flaw 23: 07-20-2003 - Hara Arena, Dayton, OH"

appearances.note: Pulls the referee out of the ring while Anubis attacks in Levond Daniels's match with Jesse Ramey.
Apologises to Denise Gomez and the crowd for how he acted at Payback and is answered with "We ain't buying it"; Ernie French later baits him in the car park and in a hallway interview.
Faces Dane Manetta backstage, later chairs him moments before his tournament match, and is thrown out of the tournament by Troy Mason for it.
Cuts a promo on the two men he has "taken out", Malik and DeVante, until Geneva and Marcus Escobar interrupt.
Comes out with Marcus Escobar to challenge blind's "mission" over the microphone and holds Marcus back from the ring.
Follows Geneva out to face blind and is stopped by her hand on his shoulder.
Rap battle with Rent-A-Hero that ends when Remix charges him and is thrown into the ringpost.
One of four new signings whom Vincent Pembridge offers short-term contracts as his "slaves", for a fight for one contract at the coming show.
With Stephen Martin, confronts Born To Die in their locker room and gets her diary back from X-Ploder.

In a locker-room scene, Hell complains that they have been passed over for the tag title shot; they interfere in the Trenchrunners' title match with Born To Die and are then heard to say they have "proven our point".
Tries to calm Hell in their locker room; comes off the top rope with a frog splash on Kid Extremo in Born To Die's title defence and lays X-Ploder's arm over him for the pin.
Angry in the locker room that other teams get the title shot; tackles Shady Suave in Born To Die's title defence, is dropped by Kid Extremo's missile dropkick and laughs with Heaven after the pin.

matches.note: A time-limit draw: "Winner: Draw".
"Winner: Brady Watts via pinfall".
"Winner: Chris McCluskey via submission to progress".

"Winner: Chris McCluskey via submission". The match follows a segment in which Thanas demands a "Loser Leaves Town match" and McCluskey refuses; McCluskey rings the bell himself and the referee starts a ten count on him mid-match. When McCluskey wins, Thanas is "the now fired Thanas" and his "four week stay in thReat had come to a premature end".
"Winners: haTE via pinfall to progress".

"Winner: Jason Semps via pinfall". Sarah Knowen stays outside the ring, hands Semps the Cruiserweight Title after the pin and holds him back when Tyler takes it back; the referee rules that no one said the title was on the line.

"Winner: Jesse Ramey via pinfall". DeVante Stevenson pulls the referee out of the ring and holds him while Anubis chokeslams Ramey and torture-racks Levond Daniels; Anubis pulls Ramey over Daniels and leaves, the referee counts, and Ramey's hand is raised.
"Winners: Jere Casarella via pinfall to progress".
"Winners: Apuro Doble via pinfall".

"Winners: Born To Die via pinfall to retain Tag Team Titles". A defence of the Tag Team Titles: Born To Die's manager Johnny Olympus, carrying the belts, argues with the referee and is thrown out before the bell; Heaven and Hell come in from the outside, Hell tackles Shady Suave and Heaven's frog splash on Kid Extremo is followed by X-Ploder's arm laid over him for the three count: "Born To Die had taken the victory with help from Heaven and Hell".
"Winners: Rent-A-Hero via pinfall to progress".

date.source: the fed's own event archive: "Sunday Night Flaw 24: 08-01-2003(07-27-2003) - Johnny Appleseed Arena, Mansfield, OH"

appearances.note: Storms into Troy Mason's office demanding to be heard while Mason stays on the phone, then smashes the phone base and the monitor; earlier furious with Vandal in a hallway, cutting him loose.
Silent in a hallway as Candor berates him and tells him he is no use, then walks away.
One of Vincent Pembridge's four newcomers, sent with Casper Cardiel to fetch coins from a vending machine and on "toilet duty".
With Race Cavanagh on Vincent Pembridge's errands, kicks a vending machine open for coins.
Cracks a chair over Phil Atken's head in the blackout in Atken's World Title match with General David Sanders, costing Sanders the match, and then chairs Sanders.
With Mary Jane and Sean Fury when R.A.T comes to tease him; he is tripped over a box and hurt.
After Louis Bourbon's win over DeVante Stevenson, comes to the ring, breaks the royal scepter over Bourbon's head and is stopped from hitting the Degree when Bourbon's retainers carry him off.
Stands silent beside Steven Fury and Mary Jane when R.A.T teases Steven.

matches.note: "Winner: Wolf via pinfall to retain Aggression Title".

Billed "Takisuma Ogama vs Jason Semps". The lights go out for Ogama's return, but it is Vincent Pembridge who comes out: "Did you pillocks actually think that Takisuma Ogama was making his return?" Pembridge puts up "BOTH my titles" against Semps and wins by the 15-count: "Winner: Vincent Pembridge via 15-count to progress and retain his titles". Semps comes out with Sarah Knowen, who advises him to back down, is sent from the ring and slides in to tend to him after the finish. Ogama never enters.
"Winner: blind via pinfall to progress".

The page disagrees with itself: its narrative gives Louis Bourbon the three count after the Revokation of Nantes and his boot-on-the-chest cover ("C'EST MOI!"), while the match's closing line reads "Winners: haTE via pinfall to progress", naming a man who is not in the match. House Show 02 recalls "after Bourbon won his match on the night". After the bell PhD comes down from the back, takes the royal scepter from Louis's carriage and breaks it across the back of the Sun King's head; as he lifts Bourbon for the Degree the retainers pull Bourbon out of the ring and carry him off, "sans carriage". PhD and the retainers act after the three count, and the narrated pin stands.

"Winner: Christian Elijah via pinfall to progress". Wolf comes out of the crowd with his Aggression Title while the referee is down, smashes it into Ernie French's face and leaves; Elijah, who had run to the ropes, connects and gets the three count.

"Winner: R.A.T via pinfall to progress". Phil Atken stands on the stage insulting the crowd and Sergey Kovhachek, who turns to answer him; Atken shouts "HE'S BEHIND YOU!" and R.A.T's boot and face driver take Sergey down for the pin, "taking advantage of Atken's interference".
"Winner: Jere Casarella via pinfall".

"Winner: Phil Atken via disqualification". A World Title match: Sanders hands the belt to the referee for "Sanders first title defense". In the blackout the Harbinger of Revenge cracks a chair over Atken's head, which "had just caused General David Sanders the match", and then chairs Sanders. The disqualification moves no belt: Sanders is still "the thReat World Champion" afterwards.

date.source: the fed's own event archive: "Sunday Night Flaw 25: 08-08-2003(08-02-2003) - Gund Arena, Cleveland, OH"

appearances.note: Billed against Chris McCluskey, but Frankie Focker fights "representing" him; comes out afterwards and chairs Focker for losing.
Slides in during Tyler Davidson's Cruiserweight Title defence against Sergey Kovhachek, bulldogs and DDTs Sergey to break his hold on Tyler, and runs back up the ramp unseen by the referee.
Kidnaps Ernie French in a car park with four henchmen in Nazi uniforms and holds him in a hideout, in scenes across the show.

Is jumped by Dane Manetta in a backstage hallway and turns it round on him, is attacked again with a chair in his locker room and left with a bloodied nose, then books a match with Manetta for Double Or Nothing.
Sends Marcus Escobar to Colin Gear with an envelope; later takes a switchblade to blind in the car park, where Marcus has chained him, until security stops her.
Given a note on his way to the ring and told his quarter-final will be next week; later beaten with a chain by Marcus Escobar in the car park.
With DeVante Stevenson and three other newcomers, storms the car park with baseball bats and chases Moe Sole round the lot with Casper Cardiel.
With DeVante Stevenson and three other newcomers, storms the car park with baseball bats and chases Moe Sole round the lot with Race Cavanagh.

matches.note: "Winner: Vincent Pembridge via knockout to retain Fighting Title". A fight in the Fighting Cage: Anubis comes in through the cage door during the blackouts with a chair, strikes Levond Daniels down and helps Pembridge to his feet; after both men's chairs land on Daniels at once, the count runs to ten.

"Winner: Tyler Davidson via pinfall to retain Cruiserweight Title". Tyler Davidson comes out with his manager (unnamed here); with Sergey Kovhachek holding Tyler in the sharpshooter, the manager is on the apron arguing with the referee, and Phil Atken slides in, bulldogs and DDTs Sergey to break the hold and runs back up the ramp unseen by the referee; Tyler then hits the Time Spike and a shooting star press for the pin.

Billed "Christian Elijah vs Chris McCluskey", but the ring announcer calls "Frankie Focker!" and the text says "Frankie was of course representing Christian Elijah who was originally scheduled to face McCluskey tonight". Focker fights and loses to a ten count on a man down in the ring, after a low blow the referee does not see: "Winner: Chris McCluskey via 10-count to progress". The narration counts the loss as Elijah's: "with that disappeared Elijah's dream"; he comes out afterwards and chairs Focker.
"Winner: haTE via pinfall to progress".

matches.stipulation: International Title Tournament Quarter-Final 3 for the thReat Fighting Championship
matches.note: "Winner: Jere Casarella via 15-count to win Fighting Title and progress". The match is fought under the Scorpion Rules, "No pinfalls; either a 15-count or a ring-out". General David Sanders comes through the crowd and slides a steel chair into the ring as the referee counts over Jere, who gets up, hits F0Rg0TTen on the chair, and the 15-count over Pembridge follows: "A new thReat Fighting champion was crowned".
"Winner: General Sanders via pinfall to retain World Title".

date.source: the fed's own event archive: "Sunday Night Flaw 26: 08-17-2003 - Toledo Sports Arena, Toledo, OH"

appearances.note: Interferes in the haTE v Chris McCluskey semi-final with a chair from ringside, hitting both men, and chairs both again after the finish.

Interferes in Jason Semps's match with Jesse Ramey, taking his Cruiserweight Title back from the ring announcer and knocking Sarah Knowen out with it; later forces Colin Gear to turn the World Title shot into the battle royal.

Gives his four henchmen the night off, finds them beaten in his locker room with "I O U One Belt" stapled to one and hunts the arena for Ernie French; then comes out when Ernie French, carrying the Aggression belt, declares him "stripped of your title" and offers him a ladder match at Double Or Nothing.

Sits on the edge of the stage clapping for R.A.T in his quarter-final with blind and chairs blind after the bell; later comes to the ring with Marcus Escobar and a blade after blind's semi-final, is whipped with the chain, and has her own blade held to her throat as blind challenges them to a handicap match at Double Or Nothing.

Comes out of the crowd after Jere Casarella's Fighting Title defence, drops from the top of the cage onto him and challenges him to "A fight to the death" at Double Or Nothing; in the car park, relives a match of his in another federation; and interferes in Jere's semi-final with blind, hitting Screwed Over on Jere and throwing blind onto him for the pin.
Comes to the ring with Geneva after blind's semi-final and swings a steel chain at him, then is beaten bloody with it.
Marcus Escobar and Geneva, "both members of the Faithless", come after blind with a chain and a blade after his semi-final and are beaten with their own weapons.
With SinFyre and their manager, watches the G.A.Y. tag match on a backstage monitor and mocks the other tag teams: "I no see any other tag team around here, right brother?"
In a mask, speaks for the Midnight Masquerade in a backstage interview before their debut and faces down Johnny Olympus; asked his name, he answers "The name is Logic, and the name is Labrytinth."
In a mask beside Logic in the Midnight Masquerade's backstage interview; lunges at Johnny Olympus and is held back by his partner.

matches.note: "Winner: Jere Casarella via knockout to retain Fighting Title". A cage fight: the ten count runs over DeVante, down in the Fighting Cage. After the finish, as Jere is handed back his title, psycho-Rio (named Rio Nexan as he strikes) comes out of the crowd, climbs the cage and drops from its top onto Jere with a twisting spinning heel kick, then challenges him to "A fight to the death" at Double Or Nothing, "One on one".

"Winner: Chris McCluskey via submission to progress". Christian Elijah hops the guard rail with a chair: his first swing hits haTE when McCluskey ducks, his second hits McCluskey, and "Since the two chair shots had evened themselves out, the referee decided against a disqualification" and gave a standing ten count. After the tap Elijah chairs haTE, by mistake again, and McCluskey.

"Winner: blind via pinfall to progress". Geneva walks out before the bell and sits on the edge of the stage, clapping for R.A.T; R.A.T's "3." is not counted because blind's leg is on the ropes. After blind's pin Geneva slaps a steel chair across his head and runs off through the crowd.

"Winner: Jesse Ramey via submission". Sarah Knowen leads Semps to the ring. Tyler Davidson comes down the ramp during the match, takes his Cruiserweight Title back from the ring announcer, rakes Semps's eyes when Semps grabs him through the ropes and knocks Sarah Knowen out with the belt; Ramey's reverse tornado DDT and the Attitude Adjustment follow, and Semps taps.
"Winner: Christian Elijah & Frankie Focker via pinfall".
"Winner: General David Sanders via pinfall to retain the World Title".

"Winner: blind via pinfall to progress". With both men down and Jere crawling to cover blind, psycho-Rio slides in, hits Jere with Screwed Over and throws blind onto him, sliding out as the referee comes to and counts the three.
"Winner: Rejection via disqualification".

matches.stipulation: Battle Royal for the #1 Contendership to the thReat World Title
matches.note: Lawrence Neumeyer (The Harbinger Of Revenge) won, "eliminating Tyler Davidson to confirm it".

date.source: the fed's own event archive: "Double Or Nothing 2003 PPV: 08-23-2003 - MGM Grand, Las Vegas, NV"

appearances.note: Referees the High Stakes Match between Sergey Kovhachek and Phil Atken and has it declared a no-contest after punching out the relief referee; earlier confronted in his office by Troy Mason.

matches.note: "Tyler Davidson via pinfall to retain the Cruiserweight Title". A no disqualification match. Tyler Davidson's manager, at ringside, shoves Semps off the top rope and holds up a chair for Tyler's leaping kick, but Sarah Knowen pulls him off the apron; he later tosses Tyler a chair. After the pin Tyler hits Semps with the belt, superkicks Sarah Knowen and powerbombs Semps onto her through a table.
"RESULT: blind via pinfall".
"No Contest due to police interference".

matches.stipulation: Fight To The Death for the thReat Fighting Title
matches.note: "RESULT: psycho-Rio via murdering Jere Casarella to win the Fighting Title".

"No Contest due to nonsensical circumstances". Colin Gear, the Commissioner, comes out in a referee's shirt and names himself "the referee of this contest". With Gear laid out by Sergey's hanging brainbuster, Atken taps to the figure-four with no referee to see it; a relief referee runs down, and a staggering Gear punches him out of the ring and has the bell rung for a no-contest. Atken then chairs Sergey, piledrives Gear onto the chair, and has the ring announcer void every stipulation: "Phil Atken is STILL a thReat employee and Sergey Kovhachek will not be forced to wear a mask".

matches.stipulation: Lumberjack Match for the thReat Aggression Title
matches.note: "Ernie French via submission to win the Aggression Title". Wolf announces the lumberjack stipulation, a deal made with Colin Gear, and his four henchmen are the lumberjacks: they beat Ernie down on the ramp and trip and chair him during the match. Ernie locks in The Croissant, Wolf refuses to submit ("Nein! No!") and fades, and the referee drops his arm three times.

Billed "Vincent Pembridge & Anubis vs Shawn Arrows & Levond Daniels"; "RESULT: Inconclusive ending". Jessica Jenkins, led to ringside on a leash by a young British man, low-blows him, slides in and kicks Anubis; the British teenager later jerks her back by the leash and clotheslines her into the guardrail. The match ends with no result after Levond Daniels shoves Shawn Arrows off the top rope and stands with Pembridge.
"Dane Manetta via being the last man standing".

matches.stipulation: Tournament Final for the thReat International Title
matches.note: "Chris McCluskey via submission to win the International Title". McCluskey comes out with Joe Soap, "his manager for the night"; Joe Soap's sudden loud burp distracts the referee so that McCluskey can drive a knee into blind's groin. blind goes limp in the Reality Check and the referee drops his arm three times.
Billed "Lawrence Neumeyer vs General David Sanders [c]"; "General David Sanders via pinfall to retain the World Title".

Goes to Vincent Pembridge's door as a missionary to save his soul, tells him that in his state he cannot beat Quinton May in ACW, and is knocked down by him.
Outside the warehouse with Tyler Davidson, complaining about not being booked and about General David Sanders paralysing Lawrence Neumeyer.

Opens the show to the warehouse crowd, books Nathan Brady and Two-Face against Vincent Pembridge, and before the main event announces the next show's World Title triple threat and the best-of-three series between blind and Phil Atken: "The first match would be PINFALLS ONLY".

"Born To Die won at 2:09 to retain the Tag Team Titles".
"Vincent Pembridge won at 9:21".
The first match of a best-of-three series for the World Title contendership; "blind won at 7:43 to take a 1-0 lead".

Ambushed with lead pipes by DeVante Stevenson and Santos Salvatore on his way in and handed to the police; attacks the two in the parking lot and is taken down by police officers in a set-up; returns from the crowd with a steel chair in the World Title match, hitting Pembridge with his own finisher and Sanders with Screwed Over.
Opens the show and beats up We Iz Special with Colin Gear in his office; in the World Title match he slides in to count Pembridge's cover of the knocked-out Sanders and stops short of three.
Strips to his boxers and dances in Troy Mason's office while Alan Abel Wade sings, and is beaten up by Mason and Colin Gear.
Sings a Britney Spears song in Troy Mason's office while Keith Anal-Wedged dances, and is beaten up by Mason and Colin Gear.
Comes to the ring with a microphone to talk about Vincent Pembridge, then spots Mormons in the crowd and screams at them until security takes her to the back.

matches.note: "Tyler Davidson won at 10:33 to retain the Cruiserweight Title".
"haTE & Christian Elijah won at 7:39".

"Chris McCluskey won at 12:21 to retain the International Title". McCluskey's hammerlock DDT gets a three count, "and Chris retained", but Vandal's foot was on the ropes, and after "viewing the evidence on the small video-wall, the referee forced the match to continue, overruling his own decision"; Vandal then taps to the Reality Check.

PhD kicked out of the Sun King's foot-on-the-chest cover into an ankle lock and "Louis tapped"; "PhD won at 9:06". Bourbon had hoisted PhD onto the top turnbuckle for the Revokation Of Nantes, a dragon suplex, then strutted before "making his equally cover; a foot on the chest of Dawson". After the bell PhD "went on to use the scepter on The Sun King again", and Bourbon's ankle "was twisted badly": he is helped to the back, and a referee tells Troy Mason that he "had really twisted his ankle".
"Phil Atken won at 9:46".

"Draw after 15:47". A defence of the World Championship. psycho-Rio, billed in it, has been taken by the police, so only Sanders and Pembridge meet. With the referee knocked out, Pembridge covers Sanders after his inverted piledriver and Troy Mason slides in to count, stopping at "THRE -": "Troy Mason effectively screwed Vincent Pembridge". psycho-Rio then jumps out of the crowd with a steel chair, hits Pembridge with his own finisher and Sanders with Screwed Over, and the referee comes to and calls the match off.

name: Malevolence

date.source: Booked on Sunday Night Flaw 12 (16 June 2002) as "Malevolence on the 23rd".

evidence.note: Jon Hackett books the card: Banderas vs Dean Bronson; CashnMoney vs Kid Jive in a "Put Up or Shut Up" tables match; Conan the Leprechaun vs Joey Starr for the number one contendership to the International Title; Jakks vs phYre; Araknis and Takisuma Ogama vs Riot for the International Title; August Monday vs Quincy Brown for the Fighting Championship; Disciple X vs "Superstar" Vince Jacobs vs Xaxon for the World Championship, "maybe the last wrestling match you fans will ever see held by thReat".
The fed's title history retires the World, International, Aggression and Fighting belts: "Belt was retired, due to closure of company on 06/23/02".
Malevolence 2003 calls itself "over a year in the making, back when thReat suddenly went on a long hiatus".

notes: Booked for the night the fed's own title history closes the company; nothing held records a result, and it may be the card that never took place.
